headline: One more run? Trade and reset? How the Lightning should handle the Kucherov situation
take:
The Athletic's piece on how Tampa Bay should handle the Nikita Kucherov situation argues that letting him walk could effectively end the Lightning's window.

Our numbers say why that's a real worry. Kucherov has 26 points in 18 games so far this season (8 goals, 18 assists), and he's not just riding a hot streak. He has scored 1.48 goals more than the quality of his chances would predict, which is a small lift, so most of this is real. At 5-on-5, TBL controls 57% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) when he's on the ice, and the team's share is 2.37 points better with him out there than without him. That's the profile of a player driving results, not just collecting them.

The team around him is strong too. TBL sits at 12-4-2 with 55% of the expected goals overall. One flag: the team's goaltending has saved 2.6 fewer goals than expected so far this season, so the margin for error is thinner than the record suggests. Losing Kucherov would take away the one piece most responsible for the chances.
